note: Ps88 the darkest psalm, unrelieved lament (Heman, 18v). Passages: the day-and-night cry v1-2; the soul among the dead v3-7; abandoned by friends v8-9; the questions to the God of the dead v10-12; the morning cry still unanswered v13-18. Human IB is almost all the anguish of the sufferer: CRY-OUT / PRAYER / CRY that gets no answer; SOUL FULL of TROUBLES; COUNTED among the dead, no STRENGTH; a HORROR to friends, SHUT-IN; eye GROWS-DIM with SORROW; AFFLICTED, SUFFERing, HELPLESS. God's wrath/waves/casting-off = qualifiers; pit/Sheol/darkness/estranged-friends imagery = standalone. Ends in darkness, no resolution - read as such.

dims.v: paired with the prayer that comes before God
v1: 'I CRY OUT (tsaaq) day and night before you' - the ceaseless cry of the sufferer, prayer that never stops though never answered.
v2: 'let my PRAYER (tephillah) come before you' - the petition begging admittance to God's presence.
v2: 'incline your ear to my CRY (rinnah)' - the loud plea, the sufferer's voice reaching for God's ear.
paired with the fullness of troubles
v3: 'For my SOUL (nephesh) is full of troubles' - the whole self saturated with affliction, the sufferer's inner state.
paired with the soul and troubles
v3: 'my soul is FULL (saba) of troubles' - satiety of suffering, filled to the brim with grief.
v3: 'full of TROUBLES (ra)' - the evils crowding the soul, life drawn near to the grave.
v4: 'I am COUNTED (chashab) among those who go down to the pit' - the sense of being already numbered with the dead, doom felt as present.
v4: 'I am a man who has no STRENGTH (eyal)' - the utter powerlessness of the sufferer, vitality gone.
v8: 'you have made me a HORROR (toebah) to them' - the sufferer become repugnant to his own, abandonment sharpened to revulsion.
v8: 'I am SHUT IN (kala) so that I cannot escape' - the trapped, walled-in despair, no way out of the affliction.
v9: 'my eye GROWS DIM (daab) through sorrow' - the wasting of the very sight, grief worn into the body.
v9: 'my eye grows dim through SORROW (oni)' - the affliction that dims the eyes, unrelenting grief.
paired with spreading out the hands
v9: 'Every day I CALL (qara) upon you, O LORD' - the daily calling that persists though heaven is silent.
v13: 'But I, O LORD, CRY (shava) to you for help' - the sufferer's persistent cry, faith holding on in the dark.
v13: 'in the morning my PRAYER (tephillah) comes before you' - the dawn petition, hope renewed each morning against the night.
paired with God hiding his face
v14: 'why do you cast my SOUL (nephesh) away?' - the self flung off, the sufferer's bewildered sense of rejection by God.
v15: 'AFFLICTED (ani) and close to death from my youth up' - a lifetime of suffering, affliction as the sufferer's whole history.
v15: 'I SUFFER (nasa) your terrors; I am helpless' - the bearing of God-sent dread, terror endured to the point of collapse.
v15: 'I am HELPLESS (pun)' - the paralysis of the terrified, undone and without recourse.
